lines.en: : Wow. It’s really coming down, isn’t it?
: I thought it was supposed to be sunny today?
: We’ll have to give that weatherman a piece of our minds, won’t we?
: When do you think it will stop?
: I’m not sure.
: Maybe never?
: Hey.
: Let’s have a talk, shall we?
: You don’t need to respond or anything. I’ll handle all of the heavy lifting since you seem pretty tied up at the moment.
: I hope you’re having a nice week. Good things are pretty hard to come by in these parts, aren’t they?
: So, let’s see here...where should I begin?
: Well, first thing’s first, it’s not very polite to touch things that don’t belong to you. And it’s especially not polite to try guessing somebody else’s password.
: What if I had some really weird stuff on my computer that made you change the way you look at me forever?
: I don’t, of course. I’m a good girl. And the only person I’ll ever have any attraction to sleeps right next door to my room, so I’d get nothing out of looking up inappropriate videos anyway.
: Hmm....what else...what else?
: Oh! There was a caterpillar on the door when I came home the other day. That was an interesting thing that happened.
: I took some pictures. Do you want to see?
: You don’t? How come?
: Wow. That’s really interesting. I had no idea you felt that way.
: So anyway, I’ve been thinking — you and I have known each other for a while now, and I think it’s about time I’m given a more important role in your life.
: Yes, I know my role is already important. But I think there’s a lot I can do that I haven’t been able to show you yet.
: And yeah, some of that is because you spend most of your time on people who aren’t me- but I’m starting to think that’s just because I’m not appealing to you the way I’m supposed to.
: Contrary to what many people believe, I am the main heroine here after all.
: I’m the first one that shows up. The first one that falls in love. And I’ve held your hand through a billion different scenarios.
: You’d be nowhere without me, whether you want to believe that or not. But sometimes, it feels like I don’t get the recognition I deserve.
: So, every once in a while, I think we should have a nice little heart-to-heart like this.
: Just to see if there’s anything one of us is doing that the other doesn’t approve of. Or something we think the other should change.
: Here. You can start. What’s something about me you want to change?
: Nothing? Really?
: Oh, come on. There’s gotta be something.
: Heheh! Now you’re just being a goober!
: But, listen — there’s something about you that I want to change.
: Or rather, there’s something about the corner you’ve pushed me into that I’m not really comfortable with anymore. So I’d appreciate it if you’d let me sort of...reposition myself, if you will.
: You see, it was never my intention to suffocate you. And I feel like, by declaring that I would stop doing that, I may have accidentally admitted I was in the wrong. Which I’m not.
: If I’m really going to be the main heroine, which I am, I think it’s only fair that I get to be treated with a little more respect. Okay?
: And the best way to respect me is by giving me a job no one else can do. A job more important than just cooking your dinner and washing your clothes.
: My dream job?
: That’s a good question. I’ve always just kind of assumed I’d be a housewife.
: But I think...if I got to choose anything in the world...
: I’d be a teacher — just like my mom.
: Wow! Now I am a teacher! It’s amazing what you can do if you really apply yourself, isn’t it?
: Anyway, today’s lesson is on “understanding.” But what I mean by that is a little more complicated than simply “getting it,” you know?
: To understand something, you need to be able to process it in a way that makes sense to you on a personal level! Because once you’re able to “relate,” you’re really able to understand.

: Now, many people may tell you that you’re able to understand things without relating to them, but those people are lying to you. And they’re normally the same people who think relatives shouldn’t have sex!
: So, if you listen to those people, you’ll wind up jaded and wrong and evil and you won’t actually “understand” anything because you were taught the wrong things before learning the right ones!
: Are you following so far?
: Great!
: Now that you understand the basics, I can begin to tell you about the first advanced principle of understanding — perception!
: We’ve touched on the topic before under similar circumstances, but I’m going to expand on it to the best of my ability! Just be gentle with me since it’s my first day on the job.
: You see, class- perception means more than just “the way a person sees something.”
: There is a hidden element to it, and that element can be dumbed down to “the way a person is made to see something.”

: This raises the question of whether or not it’s truly “perception” at all at that point because, if you’re only seeing something because you’re supposed to see it, are you really seeing anything at all?
: To provide a more specific example about what this means and how it relates to you in real life, imagine this!

: A little girl loves her uncle but her uncle is supposed to think he loves somebody else so he doesn’t love his niece as much as he’s supposed to so he’s not properly “understanding” or “perceiving” the situation.

: Because if he could understand and perceive the situation freely without interference from anyone else he’d understand and perceive that his prior misunderstood perception is...well, it’s bad! Do you get it?
: You don’t?
: Wow, this teaching thing is a lot harder than I thought it would be.
: Maybe I should just go back to being a student instead?
: That’s more like it. This is a setting I do better in.
: What’s that? You think there’s something wrong with the class? Well, that’s probably just because you’re not “understanding” what’s going on right now! Hahah! Do you see what I did there?
: I made a joke and this is the part where you’re supposed to praise me for it.
: Sensei, can I go to the bathroom to watch a concert or whatever?
: This is stupid. I play the violin.
: I’m Ami! Champion of Justice and whatever!
: When my butler hears about this, he’s going to give me a gun.
: Everyone be quiet, you are interrupting my learning.
: What’s that?
: You’re having a hard time following the dialogue since all of us are Ami?
: I guess I can see how that might start problems. But I think you’ve got bigger fish to fry since you’re the one who has to teach us about understanding now.
: It’s hard, isn’t it?
: But the reason for that is kind of simple. And it calls back that other thing I was talking about when I was trying my hand at being a teacher — that’s how you’re supposed to be.
: You don’t need to get everything and you won’t get everything because you’re not allowed to get everything. So be happy with some things since all things are off limits.
: Well, all things except Ami of course. You can have as much Ami as you want. So you should go ahead and want more Ami.
: Oooooooh. That’s what it means to understand something? That’s way simpler than how I was teaching it. It was a little lacking in terms of incestual anecdotes, though.
: Hm?
: Oh. That’s probably just because you’re blaming yourself for what happened in the hallway.
: teenagers.
: You shouldn’t blame yourself, Sensei. It’s only natural to get upset and start thinking irrationally when you see something that scares you.
: Or at least it would be natural for most people. Your truth is that fear is alluring. It excites you in a way it’s not supposed to. And that’s something I can relate to.
: I might be a good girl, but that doesn’t mean I don’t do bad things every once in a while.
: But that’s okay. Because soon, I won’t have to do anything bad ever again and you’ll be mine forever and ever and ever and ever and ever and no one else will see you.
: You are safe inside your box.
: don’t open the door
: Do you ever wonder where we go when we die?
: Grandma believed in Heaven. Mom too near the end. And you already know my thoughts on the matter from our bus ride backwards.
: It might not make the most sense from a logical standpoint, but it definitely sounds the nicest. And I like to think the two of them are hanging out up there and playing bingo or something.
: Anyway, Maya never actually killed a kitten and the white car was ours. Are you close to waking up yet?
: I hope not. But at the same time, I hope so because I’m not sure how much more of this I can take before I throw myself off of the roof.

: You see, you hurt me a lot. All of you have been hurting me lately. It’s like you have a collective fetish for making cute redheads sad. And I try not to kink shame, but I’m not a big fan of that one.
: What’s my biggest kink? I don’t have any. I’m a good girl. And incest doesn’t count. I just like knowing that if I bite my partner’s neck, the blood I’ll draw will be my own.
: And no, I’m not a vampire. But it would be really cool if I was so I could stop aging and not run the risk of you getting less attracted to me as time goes on.
: Not like that’s ever going to happen in the first place. But, let’s face it, we both know this is the me you’ll like best. And I don’t blame you at all for that.
: I wouldn’t blame you for liking the littler me either. Especially after doing the same thing to your computer that you did to mine and learning you’re even worse than everyone thinks you are.
: And they think you’re gross, Sensei. Even if they want you to fuck them, they think you’re gross. They’re probably just wet from all the hormones and the fact that you’re super attractive.
: But they all hate you and think you’re gross. Which is why you should love me and only me because I don’t think you’re gross. I think you’re awesome.
: Rain King.

: I CAN’T FUCKING TAKE IT ANYMORE!!!
: NOTHING I DO WORKS AND YOU KEEP FALLING FURTHER AND FURTHER AWAY!!!
: WHAT DO I NEED TO DO TO MAKE YOU MINE AGAIN?!?!?! TELL ME! TELL ME TELL ME TELL ME!
: Wow. It’s really coming down, isn’t it?
: Everything you can imagine is real.
: Why not imagine God?
: Yuu! I’m coming in!
: Why didn’t you answer the door? I thought you were dead in here.
: If I was dead, I definitely wouldn’t have answered the door.
: Yuu! I’m coming in too!
: Don’t let-
: Come in!
: slip.
: I seriously hate you.
: You have too many strong opinions concerning doors today.
: Yeah, whatever. Listen, I-
: Sorry, Miu. Someone’s at the door and if I don’t answer it, they’ll think I’m dead. I don’t want to risk that.
: I can’t believe this is actually happening right now.
: Come in, mysterious door friends.
: Wow! Look at this place, Kanon! It’s tiny, but it’s way nicer than the sewer! And super clean too!
: Nii-sama will love it. Go fetch him, Tsurumi. Have him bring the chains as well.
: Sorry, ladies. This place isn’t for sale- but you wouldn’t want it anyway. Aliens have already attacked the neighbors and it’s possible they’ll be coming for me next.
: Sorry, Saki.
: Wow. It’s really coming down, isn’t it?
: I thought it was supposed to be sunny today?
: History repeats itself. That much is common knowledge.
: But here, in this most special of places, no lines will ever be the exact same length.
: It’s the little differences that help us understand where we are. And we can map them out like coordinates on our way to an unwanted escape.
: Heaven is real, Sensei.
: I have seen it.
: It’s closer than you think.
: Don’t open the door.
: Stay home forever and you’ll never hurt anyone again.
: I’ll be with you all the while.
: I am your little girl.
: And you are my-
